column1: # Fork probes: does each fork change / bug still differ from upstream?
# Tab-separated: id <TAB> kind <TAB> path <TAB> pattern <TAB> note
# ids: B-* are the bug/fix ledger ids from BUGS.md (one row per ledger entry).
#      P-* are probe-only rows for fork features/files with no ledger entry.
# kind:
#   fix   pattern is our fix's signature.  found in upstream = merged upstream,
#         our patch is now redundant (delete it at the next sync).
#         not found = still fork-only, patch still needed.
#   bug   pattern is the *buggy* code.  found in upstream = bug still present
#         upstream (candidate for an upstream issue).  not found = gone.
#   file  existence check: does upstream have something at this fork-only path?
#         rows carry NO pattern column (`id<TAB>file<TAB>path<TAB>note`) because a
#         tab is IFS whitespace and `read` collapses runs of it, so an empty
#         field cannot be expressed; answered with `git cat-file -e`.
#   feature  pattern is a fork feature's signature.  found in upstream = they
#         shipped the same thing (expect conflicts); not found = still ours.
# Patterns are matched literally (`grep -FQ`) against `git show <upstream>:<path>`.
# Keep them short, distinctive, and true to the current upstream base: a probe
# that rots silently is worse than no probe, so re-check after each sync.
